# Stake Solana

> Stake Solana by delegating SOL to a validator or holding a liquid staking token to earn staking rewards.

## Pages
- [Stake Solana](https://insert_url/): Native delegation, liquid staking, reward calculations, fees, unstaking, and frequently asked questions.
- [SOL staking APR](https://insert_url/#rewards): Interactive net APR calculator with gross APR, validator commission, and liquid staking pool reward fees.
- [SOL unstaking](https://insert_url/#unstaking): Native deactivation, epoch boundaries, withdrawal, and liquid staking exits.

## Staking methods
Native delegation places SOL in a stake account controlled by its stake and withdrawal authorities. Each stake account delegates to one validator. Liquid staking issues a transferable token representing a claim on a pool's stake.

## Reward calculations
Native net APR = gross APR multiplied by (1 minus validator commission).
Liquid net APR = gross APR multiplied by (1 minus validator commission) multiplied by (1 minus pool reward fee).
Annual SOL rewards = staked SOL multiplied by net APR. Divide the annual result by 12 for the monthly average. Percentages are converted to decimals for multiplication.
The calculator starts with 100 SOL, 6.5% gross APR, and 5% validator commission: 6.175% net APR and 6.175 SOL in annual rewards before compounding and transaction or entry/exit fees. The editable liquid pool fee starts at 2%, giving 6.0515% net APR with the same other inputs. Rates vary by epoch.

## Fees and timing
The network base fee is 5,000 lamports per signature plus any priority fee. Stake accounts also require a rent-exempt reserve. Native activation and deactivation follow epoch boundaries; an epoch is roughly 2-3 days. Network cooldown capacity can extend unstaking over multiple epochs. Inactive stake is withdrawn in a separate transaction. A liquid staking token can be swapped subject to liquidity, market price, and slippage; pool redemption follows its own schedule.

## Security
Review native stake and withdrawal authorities, validator performance, and commission. For liquid staking, review token mint addresses, contracts, audits, upgrade controls, and redemption terms. SOL price, validator performance, smart contracts, and market liquidity affect staking positions.
